hints.title: Word Graph Shortest Path Obstacle
hints.text: Finding the shortest transformation sequence by comparing every pair of words takes O(N^2 * L) time, which times out on thousands of words. How can generating 26 single-letter mutations locate neighbors in O(26 * L) per word?

hints.title: Bidirectional Boundary Wave Invariant
hints.text: Expanding from the smaller frontier towards the other frontier minimizes the branching exponent, stopping as soon as the forward and backward frontiers intersect.

hints.title: Two-End Frontier Expansion Procedure
hints.text: Convert wordList into a set. If endWord is absent, return 0. Maintain two frontiers: begin_set containing beginWord and end_set containing endWord. At each step, expand the smaller set: for each word, mutate each character with all 26 lowercase letters. If mutated word is in opposite set, return step count + 1. If in word set, record in next set and remove from word set.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of words in wordList (1 <= N <= 5000)
L: length of each word (1 <= L <= 10)
complexity.notes: Bidirectional expansion limits explored vertices to O(b^(d/2)) where b is the branching factor.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Building an explicit adjacency graph via pairwise word comparisons takes quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Set membership achieves constant-time string lookup at the cost of O(N * L) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using bidirectional frontier swapping to dramatically reduce expansion branching factor.
